decision: Wire scripts/steward_collect_browser_render.js into the scheduled steward workflow (installing Chromium for it) so the browser-render sensor is evaluated on every run?
whyItMatters: The sensor reports not-evaluated without a fresh browser-render input, so rendered frontend facts stay unobserved on scheduled runs. Adding the step changes the workflow's dependencies and runtime.
evidence: Run locally on 2026-10-28 it rendered 95 pages x 2 viewports in about 4 minutes and found 29 pages with rendered defects the static sensor cannot see.
The collector serves docs/ from a local static server and aborts every external request unsent.
Frontend fixes remain human-gated (CLAUDE.md); this only observes.

Founder rulings batch 1, 2026-11-06, relayed to the Steward owner (Opus) for #2283 (verbatim): "Headless is free to use anytime. real browser requires a "steward setting" to be on--meaning normally when I run a founder steward run, I'll say that browser is available or not. Normally its not. So keep this at config level, default headless always on."

Ruling as applied: Headless Chromium on by default for scheduled and founder Steward runs; real/interactive browser only behind an explicit run-scoped Steward setting (default OFF); unavailable collection reported accurately, never healthy.
recommended: Headless Chromium on by default for scheduled and founder Steward runs; real/interactive browser only behind an explicit run-scoped Steward setting (default OFF); unavailable collection reported accurately, never healthy.
alternative: Keep it an operator-run collector until a quarter of local runs shows low noise.
